sentences.text: Petitioners have filed the petition U/sec.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, claiming compensation amount of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest from the respondents.

2. Petitioners case is as Follows:
Petitioner no.1 is the wife petitioner no.2,3 are the Parents of the deceased Hariprakash S/o. D. Srinivasan

That on 18.01.2024 at about 10.25 pm, Hariprakash S, was a driving the motorcycle bearing Reg No.KA-53-HT-8371, in Kolar-Bengaluru highway, near Yele Mallappashetty lake, wherein the driver of the TATA Canter beg.

Reg. No.KA-01-AF-4709, has negligently parked the said vehicle, without any signal in the road, as a result two wheeler colluded with the said Lorry, in the accident,
Hariprakash S, sustained grievous injuries and he died due to the accidental injuries.
Autopsy of conducted in Government hospital at Hoskote.
Petitioners have performed funeral and obsequies as per their customs and they have spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- for the same.

3. Petitioners alleged that deceased was 33 yeas of age as on the date of accident and prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and he was working as IT dealer and was earning Rs.50,000/- per month and he was the only earning member for their family.

They alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle and the Jurisdictional police have registered the case against the driver of the aforesaid offending vehicle in Cr.No.23/2024.

Petitioners alleged that the respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle and the respondent No.1 is the insurer, accordingly they are jointly liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and they prays this tribunal to award the compensation amount with interest by allowing the petition.
4. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, Respondent no.2 has not chosen to appear before this tribunal and he placed exparte.
Respondent No.1 appeared through its counsel filed vakalath and written statement by denying the entire version of the petition in toto.
Respondent No.1 has specifically denied the age, income of the deceased.
Respondent No.1 contended that insured has violated the policy conditions and accident occurred due to the negligent act of the deceased and prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.

5. In order to prove the case, the Petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW-1, and examined the another witness as PW-2, produced and marked 23 documents which are at Ex.P1 to 23 and they are fully cross examined.
6. Respondent No.1 examined its official RW-1 produced and marked two documents, which are at Ex.D-1 & 2 and he is fully cross examined.
7. I have heard the arguments form the counsels appearing for both the sides.
I have perused the entire records.

sentences.text:
On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners prove that on 18.01.2024 at about 10.25 pm, Hariprakash S, was a driving the motorcycle bearing Reg No.KA-53-HT-8371, in Kolar-Bengaluru highway, near Yele Mallappashetty lake, wherein the driver of the TATA Canter beg.
Reg. No.KA-01-AF-4709, has negligently parked the said vehicle, without any signal in the road, as a result two wheeler colluded with the said Lorry, in the accident, Hariprakash S, sustained grievous injuries and he died due to the accidental injuries as alleged in the petition.?
2.
Whether respondent no.1 proves that insured has violated the policy conditions and Hariprakash died due to his negligent act as contended in the written statement.
3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
4.
What order
or award?

9. After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
 Issue no.1 & 3: In the Affirmative,
 Issue no.2 : in the negative  Issue no.4 : as per final order  for the following:
 REASONS 10. Issues No.1 to 3 :- I have taken both the issues together for common discussion, so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW.1 being the petitioner no.1 and wife of the deceased Hariprakash S, S/o. Srinivasan she reiterated the petition averments in her examination-in-chief affidavit.
In the cross examination of PW-1, she admitted that she is working and earning.
11. According to the petitioners, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving/act of the driver of the offending vehicle.

In order to prove the actionable negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle, Petitioners have tendered the FIR, Mahazars, sketch, Inquest, PM report, final report, which are at Ex.P1 to 7 & 10.
12.

On perusal of the aforesaid undisputed documents it is evident that Hariprakash S/o.Srinivasan died in the motor vehicle road accident caused by the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle that is Manju S/o. Guddappa.

Further, Ex.P-9 is the reply notice given by the respondent No.2 to the notice issued U/s 133 of IMV Act, wherein he admit that his driver was having valid DL and the policy of the vehicle was valid as on the date of the accident.

In the cross examination of Kavita Kashinath Chowgule vs Sbi General Ins Co Ltd on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152125151/
3 PW-1, nothing worth is elicited to disbelieve the petitioner version.

sentences.text: Respondent No.1 has failed to establish its contention that insured has violated the policy condition and accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased.
Further more final report which is at Ex.P.10 is filed after thorough investigation and it is not disputed by the respondents as such it has attained the finality.
Hence, the version of the petitioner based on the evidence can not be ignored and unsubstantiated contention of the respondent no.1 can not be accepted.

13. Petitioners have examined the HR of Solera Company, he deposed that Hariprakash, S/o.
Srinivasan was working in their company as analyst and his oral testimony collaborates with Ex.P-15, 16 that is appointment letter and payslips.
As per the payslip for the month of January-2024 the gross salary of the Hariprakash was Rs.96,183/-.

Admittedly he was an income tax access, if IT is computed on new regime for the financial year 2023-24 Hariprakash has to pay Rs.9,388/- as income tax including the cess of 4% and he has to pay professional tax of Rs.200/- per month.

Accordingly, after deducting the aforesaid income tax amount, the monthly income of the deceased is assessed as Rs.86,595/-.
14.
Further more as per the entry in Aadhar card of the deceased which is Ex.P.11, the date of birth of the deceased is 18.05.1990.
Accordingly the age of the deceased as on the date of the accident was 33 years 8 months and multiplier 16 is applicable.
15. Deceased was self employee, married and he was below 40 years, accordingly 40% should be added towards his monthly income for future prospectus.
Deceased left behind 3 dependents accordingly 1/3 should be deducted from his monthly income towards his personal expenses.

16. The loss of dependency is calculated as follows:
1 Monthly income Rs. 86,595/-
Add: 40% of income future prospectus Rs. 34,638/-

Monthly income Rs. 1,21,233/-
2 Less; 1/3 for personal expenses Rs. 40,411/-
3 Monthly income Rs. 80,822/-
Rs.12,467 (income)X 12 (month) X 16 Rs.1,55,17,824/- (Multiplier ) Accordingly petitioners are entitled for Rs.1,55,17,824/- as compensation under the head Loss of Dependency.
17. Loss of estate;

As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranaya sethi case, Tribunal has to award Rs.15,000/- as compensation under this head.
18 . Funeral Expenses, transportation etc.,

Accordingly as per the judgment in Praneya sethi case,
minimum amount of Rs.15,000/- can be awarded under this head.

Except the aforesaid compensation amount, petitioners are not entitled for compensation in any other heads.
20. In total the petitioners are entitled for compensation as follows;
Sl Compensation
under the Head
Amount No. 1 Loss of dependency Rs.1,55,17,824/-

2 Loss of estate Rs. 15,000/-
3 Funeral expenses & transportation Rs. 15,000/- 4 Loss of Consortium Rs. 1,20,000/-
TOTAL Rs.1,56,67,824/-

21. Rate of Interest:

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

sentences.text: Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.A on the compensation amount form the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
22. Liability:

Admittedly the validity of the insurance policy of the offending vehicle is not disputed nor denied by the respondent No.1 and they have not probabilise their contention, accordingly Respondent No.1 being the insurer has to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioners.
Accordingly respondent no.1 is directed to pay the compensation amount along interest before this tribunal with in one month from the date of the Judgment.
Accordingly I am answering Issue no.1 & 3 in the affirmative, Issue No.2 in the negative.
23. Issue No.4:
For the foregoing reason and discussion, on the aforesaid issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is allowed with cost.

Petitioners are entitled for compensation amount of Rs.1,56,67,824/- with interest @
6% p.a. from the date of claim petition, till realization.
The respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of the judgment.
